title: The intelligible-principle test
summary: The test asks whether Congress supplied a guiding policy or standard for the exercise of delegated authority.
notes:
Identify the delegated task by interpreting the whole statute, then assess the guidance Congress imposed. Hampton names the formulation and upholds bounded tariff adjustments. Schechter rejects an exceptionally broad economic code-making power with little meaningful guidance. Yakus, Whitman, and the Gundy plurality illustrate the willingness to accept substantial discretion when statutory purposes, defined subjects, and standards constrain it.

A statute need not mechanically dictate every outcome. Whitman explains that the amount of acceptable discretion varies with the breadth of the authority, and that voluntary agency restraint cannot repair a constitutional failure by Congress. Gundy also shows the importance of opinion alignment: the judgment sustained the statute, but only four Justices joined Kagan’s full statutory and constitutional explanation.
